svg.text: Sinusoidal (v2) against RoPE (v2.5): the same sin and cos, used two ways
both build clock hands from sin and cos, with speeds from one formula — v2 ADDS its hand to the word’s numbers once, at the start; v2.5 TURNS q and k by it, inside attention
① The code — both start from sin and cos of (position × speed)
speed of pair i = 10000^(−2i / 512): 256 speeds, one for each pair of the word’s 512 numbers — pair 0 turns 57.3° per word
The last line is the whole use: the table’s numbers are added to the word’s numbers.
speed of pair i = 10000^(−2i / 128): 64 speeds, one for each pair of a head’s 128 numbers — the same formula (v2’s pairs 0, 4, 8, …)
The last line is the whole use: each pair (x1, x2) of q and k is turned by the angle.
② The same clocks — pair 0 at positions 0 to 15 (5 is “cat”, 15 is “floor”): up to here the two ways are one
pair 0 of the table at each position: the point (sin p, cos p) is the tip of a hand of length 1,
57.3° further round per word (clockwise, because the table writes sin first — that changes nothing)
pair 0 of the turn at each position: the angle p × 57.3°,
③ What happens to the word — “cat” at 5 and “floor” at 15, pair 0 (v2: the word’s own numbers; v2.5: its q and k, head 0)
Adding changes the hand’s direction AND its length, by amounts set by the positions
themselves (5 and 15): what reaches attention is word and place mixed together.
Turning keeps each hand’s length; its direction moves by position × 57.3°, so between
the two hands only the difference is left: (15 − 5) × 57.3°.

pair 0 of v2’s table at positions 0 to 15: number 0 is sin(position), number 1 is cos(position) — the usual picture draws them as waves, one number at a time

text.style: fill:var(--s3);font-family:'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Courier New', monospace;font-size:11px;font-weight:600;text-anchor:start

svg.text: every point lies on the circle, because sin² + cos² = 1:
the pair is ONE clock hand of length 1, 57.3° further round per position
Waves show one number at a time against position. The clock shows the two numbers of a pair together — and attention always multiplies pairs with pairs:
a pair’s share of a score is length × length × cos(angle between). So the clock is the picture of what attention actually feels; on the waves, a length or an angle is invisible.

text.tspan: The difference only shows in pairs
, adding the position hand to the word’s hand changes both the direction AND the length. In

After the weights W_k mix all 512 numbers, the table’s steady 57.3° turn is gone: the hand only wobbles (within 22°).
Its length runs from 1.72 to 2.34 — set by the seat alone.
Turned by position × 57.3°: exactly one step further round at each place.
Its length is 0.83 everywhere — the seat never changes it.

the table at position 15 is the table at position 5 turned by 10 × 57.3° — a property the Transformer’s authors counted on; follow it through the addition
① Follow the turn from 5 to 15 — first on its own, then with the word

a pure turn — the same one
The 2017 authors chose this table partly for (a): a fixed gap is a fixed turn, so the model
could learn relative positions from it. But (b) is what the model receives: adding the word
bends the turn out of shape, and the model has to learn to dig it back out.
RoPE (2021) keeps the very same turn and applies it to the word’s own q and k,
instead of adding it. (b) stays a pure turn, so the gap arrives clean — in every
Why each way was the fix of its time
the same sin and cos, two inventions four years apart — each solved the problem in front of it and left the next one open
